name: Positron-Electron Tandem Ring Accelerator
notes: The DESY anniversary page says PETRA served as pre-accelerator for HERA "starting in 1986"; Bethke & Wagner (Eur. Phys. J. H 2022) say PETRA "came back to life in 1990 as PETRA-II" after the November 1986 shutdown. The record follows the latter for the collider/pre-accelerator distinction and only models the collider period.
PETRA II (HERA pre-accelerator) and PETRA III (synchrotron-radiation source) are not separate records here; photon science is outside the Atlas scope (A26).

summary.plain: DESY's 2.3-kilometre electron-positron ring in Hamburg, which collided beams from 1978 to 1986. Experiments there (TASSO, MARK J, JADE, PLUTO, CELLO) found the first direct evidence of the gluon in three-jet events in 1979.
summary.technical: PETRA e⁺e⁻ storage-ring collider, 2304 m circumference, beam energy up to 23.39 GeV (centre-of-mass up to about 46.8 GeV); first collisions September 1978, final collider shutdown 3 November 1986. Four collision regions: TASSO, MARK J, JADE and PLUTO (replaced by CELLO in March 1980). Later reused as HERA pre-accelerator and as the PETRA III light source.
